instruction: Identify all slide numbers that contain the word "Prompt" and save these slide numbers to a text file named "prompt_slides.txt" on Desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding slide numbers containing the word 'Prompt' and saving them to text file. Evaluator checks if the expected slide numbers (1, 12, 13, 20, 23, 25, 26) are present in the output. Verified by analyzing PPTX: slides with 'Prompt' include slide 1 (title), 12 ('Crafting Effective Prompts'), 13 ('One Prompt'), 20 ('Principles' listing 'One Prompt'), 23 ('Prompt Library'), 25 ('about crafting prompts'), and 26 ('Craft a prompt').

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts numbers from the text file using regex pattern \d+, which appropriately captures slide numbers
Metric function correctly handles 'type: rule' expected parameter - uses expected.get('numbers') to access the rules dict returned by get_rule
Expected values are semantically correct and verified against actual PPTX content (metadata documents which slides contain 'Prompt')
Evaluator provides complete coverage of the instruction requirement - checks that all required slide numbers are saved to the file
Partial credit logic is reasonable - returns ratio of found expected numbers

Minor issue: Metric only checks if expected numbers are present but doesn't penalize false positives (extra incorrect slide numbers). A file with [1, 5, 12, 13, 20, 23, 25, 26] would score 1.0 even though slide 5 shouldn't be there
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts list of numbers → metric verifies expected numbers are present in that list
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding logic to penalize false positives: check that result doesn't contain unexpected numbers, or use set equality comparison instead of subset checking
Could improve metric to return 0.0 if extra numbers are present beyond expected ones, ensuring only exact matches get full score
